findings.issue_text: Routes for member add/remove are declared as bare member routes inside resources :groups, so they generate :id params, but the controller reads params.require(:group_id), causing ActionController::ParameterMissing in production
Controller specs invoke actions directly and bypass route parameter recognition, so they don't catch the :group_id vs :id routing mismatch
totalPages calculation using Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1 is off by one when user_count is an exact multiple of limit, producing a trailing empty page and incorrect showingLast value

remove_member deletes the group membership immediately via group.users.delete(user_id) but then reports success/failure based on an unrelated group.save call, causing inconsistent client/server state if save fails after the deletion already succeeded
usernames input field is not cleared after successfully adding members, causing stale usernames to be resent on subsequent submissions
No test coverage (e.g. assert_routing or integration/request spec) exercises the actual DELETE/PUT /admin/groups/:id/members routes to catch the group_id vs id param mismatch
New pagination behavior in groups_controller.rb#members (limit/offset defaults, meta.total/limit/offset payload shape) has no spec coverage

goldens.comment: The findMembers() call is now asynchronous and unhandled. The controller may not have member data immediately available, creating a race condition.

In the next action, capping the next offset at user_count can produce an empty page (e.g., total equal to limit results in offset == total, showing 2/2 with no members). This can cause confusing UX on the last page.
The remove_member test uses xhr :put to call the remove_member action, but the route defines delete 'members' => 'groups#remove_member' requiring DELETE method.

The `totalPages` calculation using `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` produces an extra page when `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit`, leading to incorrect pagination. For example, with 100 users and a limit of 50, it reports 3 pages instead of 2, allowing navigation to an empty page.
Expected to return a value at the end of function - code paths without explicit returns will return undefined

The route provides the group's ID in params[:id], but the code attempts to read it from params[:group_id], causing the action to fail. This results in a broken feature when trying to access group memberships.

adjudication_records.issue_text: remove_member deletes the group membership immediately via group.users.delete(user_id) but then reports success/failure based on an unrelated group.save call, causing inconsistent client/server state if save fails after the deletion already succeeded

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::GroupsController#remove_member, the code performs `group.users.delete(user_id)` (which issues the join-table delete immediately) and then decides whether to render success based on `group.save`. That `save` is not coupled to the membership deletion and can fail independently (validations/callbacks/DB issues), in which case the controller would return an error even though the membership row was already deleted. Conversely, it may return success even if `delete` removed nothing (user wasn’t a member). This mismatch is a real correctness issue in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: usernames input field is not cleared after successfully adding members, causing stale usernames to be resent on subsequent submissions

adjudication.rationale: In `admin-group.js.es6`, the `addMembers` action calls `this.get("model").addMembers(this.get("usernames"));` and does not reset/clear the `usernames` property afterward. The template binds the `user-selector` component to `usernames=usernames`, so unless the component clears it internally (not shown in this diff), the entered usernames will remain in the controller state. The code even includes a `// TODO: should clear the input` comment, corroborating that the input is currently not cleared. This can lead to the same usernames being submitted again on a subsequent click.

New pagination behavior in groups_controller.rb#members (limit/offset defaults, meta.total/limit/offset payload shape) has no spec coverage

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change GroupsController#members to always use limit/offset and to return a new JSON shape with members + meta (total/limit/offset). However, the proposed finding claims this new pagination/payload behavior has *no spec coverage*. From the diff alone we can only verify that no new spec was added/modified for GroupsController#members; we cannot verify that there are no existing specs elsewhere already covering this endpoint. Therefore the claim is not strictly verifiable as a real defect from the provided diff.
